newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: CEPA bid seen possible for Malaysia's YTL.
newsitem.headline: CEPA bid seen possible for Malaysia's YTL.

text.p: Malaysia's YTL Corp Bhd could be set to announce that it has entered the bidding for a stake in Hong Kong's Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA), dealers and analysts said on Tuesday.
Officials at YTL, an infrastructure developer and power concern, were not available for comment on Tuesday.
The company has called a 5 p.m. (0900 GMT) news conference but has not given the topic. However, a source close to the company said it concerned the CEPA negotiations.
YTL's stock was down 30 cents to 14.20 ringgit at 0315 GMT.
CEPA's parent Hopewell Holdings Ltd has agreed to sell most of its 60 percent stake to the U.S. utility Southern Co's Southern Electric International.

Azman Mohktar, an energy analyst at UBS Research, said YTL likely would need help to buy the controlling stake in CEPA. The bid is expected to be valued at 6.5 billion ringgit for most of the stake, he said.
"YTL alone can't swallow CEPA, but with the Malaysian government's help, this can be done," he said.
A report on Tuesday by Jupiter Securities said YTL would have to put up more than $1.6 billion for the controlling stake in CEPA. YTL has a market capitalisation of $3.3 billion, it said.
"Any bid by YTL at a price higher than that offered by Southern Co is seen as excessive and unwarranted and we maintain our view that the stock (of YTL) is fully valued," the report said.
